idea-plugin.name: CommentCloak
idea-plugin.description:
Hide AI noise. Keep what matters.

AI-generated code comes with AI comments. Copilot, Claude, Cursor and friends narrate every step — // Increment the counter by one sitting directly above counter++. Individually harmless, collectively they double the height of every file and bury the three comments that actually explain something. CommentCloak is a comment filter for exactly that: it cloaks the narration and leaves the signal.

How it works. CommentCloak does not rewrite anything. It collapses code comments using the editor's own fold regions — the same mechanism the IDE uses to fold imports and method bodies. Nothing is deleted, nothing is reformatted, the file on disk is untouched and version control sees no change at all. Toggle it back off and every comment reappears exactly where it was. Hover a marker to peek at the text it stands for, or click it to reveal that one comment — it cloaks itself again once your caret leaves it.

Features

  • One-key toggle — Ctrl+Alt+/ to hide or show comments everywhere at once. The setting is remembered across restarts.
  • Right-click menu entry in the editor, plus an entry in the View menu.
  • Status bar switch showing Comments: hidden / Comments: shown — click it to flip.
  • Keeps what matters: TODO, FIXME, HACK, XXX, BUG and NOTE stay visible.
  • Keeps tool directives: eslint-disable, @ts-ignore, @ts-expect-error, noinspection, noqa, prettier-ignore, biome-ignore, region markers and more.
  • Keeps license headers: Copyright, SPDX-License, @license, @preserve.
  • Keeps only the paragraph that matters: in a fifteen-line block with a single TODO buried in it, CommentCloak keeps the TODO paragraph and hides the essay around it instead of leaving the whole block on screen.
  • Compact marker: a hidden block collapses to a small rounded pill showing the CommentCloak icon and how many lines it stands for — drawn on the comment's own lines, so nothing above it moves. Prefer the stock fold placeholder? Switch the marker style in the settings.
  • Documentation comments too — AI assistants love essay-length JSDoc blocks, so /** … */ is cloaked by default; one checkbox keeps JSDoc / KDoc / docstrings visible if you prefer.
  • Per-kind filters: choose independently whether to fold comments that are line (//, #, --), block (/* … */), documentation (/** … */) or HTML (<!-- … -->).
  • Minimum length filter — keep the one-liners, hide only the essay-style explanations an assistant left behind.
  • Regex keep-list — add your own patterns; anything matching is never hidden.
  • Whole-line collapsing — consecutive comment lines fold into a single small placeholder, taking their line breaks and indentation with them, so no blank gaps remain.
  • Caret aware — the comment you are editing is never folded out from under your cursor. Click a marker to reveal a comment; it cloaks itself again once your caret leaves it, so nothing you open stays open by accident.
  • Works everywhere — IntelliJ IDEA, WebStorm, PyCharm, GoLand, Rider, PhpStorm, RubyMine, CLion, DataGrip and Android Studio, in any language whose parser produces comment tokens: TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Java, Kotlin, Go, C#, Rust, PHP, Ruby, SQL, YAML, HTML and the rest.

Keywords: hide comments, fold comments, comment filter, code comments, AI comments, AI-generated code.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.1.0

  • First release.
  • Global hide/show toggle bound to Ctrl+Alt+/, with entries in the View menu and the editor context menu.
  • Status bar widget showing and flipping the current state.
  • Per-kind filters for line, block, documentation and HTML comments.
  • Default keep-list for TODO/FIXME/HACK, linter and compiler directives, region markers and license headers; fully editable as regular expressions.
  • Minimum-length filter and configurable placeholder.
  • Consecutive comment lines merge into one fold; whole-line collapsing leaves no gaps.
  • Partial hiding: a block comment that matches a keep pattern keeps only the matching paragraph and hides the rest.
  • Compact pill marker with the line count, or the classic fold placeholder.
  • Caret-aware folding: revealed comments re-cloak when the caret leaves them, and the markers are repaired after the IDE's own folding passes.

action.description: CommentCloak: visually hide code comments — files are never modified
